operator_io_quirks: All identifiers are simple ASCII with no spaces; only mixed case (Player_ID, Club_ID, Big_Silver, Starting_year) — quoting with " is still required.
Tiny tables (player=14, club=6, coach=5, player_coach=7, match_result=6): no huge-table sampling path exercised; original_values fit fully.
FKs use backtick-quoted parent refs in DDL (`club`(`Club_ID`)) — pragma foreign_key_list resolves them fine; no dangling FKs.
player_coach and match_result have composite PKs (Player_ID,Coach_ID) and (Rank,Club_ID) — composite-PK member max_l0=30 path applies.
coach.Club_ID has only 2 distinct values (1,3) though club has 6 rows — FK parent is non-unique-valued in practice (sparse coverage).
player_coach.Player_ID distinct=7 but player has 14 rows; player_coach.Coach_ID distinct=4 of 5 — FK coverage is partial, not full.
No self-references, no NOT NULL, no CHECK, no UNIQUE constraints, no views/triggers/indexes in DDL.
All columns storage class matches declared type (INT->integer, TEXT->text); no type-affinity contradictions.
Rank appears as TEXT in player ('1st','2nd') and INT in coach/match_result — same name, different declared type across tables.
Gender is TEXT with 2 distinct values ('M','F') in both player and coach — low-cardinality enum-like.
Sponsor_name contains em-dash (—) and accented chars (Bouché, Häcken, Djurgården) — non-ASCII text values.
Start_year/Starting_year are INT holding year-like values (2009, 2010) — declared INT so Number fuzzer, not Date.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on all INT columns: range [-10^scale,10^scale] with scale from type args (none -> default), so Player_ID/Club_ID/Votes/Gold/Points draw huge ints far outside original 1..14 / 5..14355.
String fuzzer on all TEXT columns: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings length 0..20 plus contaminate suffix/prefix — Player_name, Club_name, Region, Occupation become gibberish, losing the real names.
Gender (TEXT, 2 distinct) gets random strings, not 'M'/'F' — ENUM semantics lost; queries filtering Gender='M' likely return empty or wrong.
Rank TEXT ('1st'..'4th') gets random strings; Rank INT (coach/match_result) gets huge ints — cross-table Rank joins/comparisons break.
Composite PKs (player_coach, match_result) get fresh random ints per column then PK-duplicate drop — few rows survive, FK consistency to player/coach/club may be lost after filtering.
FK fill draws from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement; coach.Club_ID only 2 distinct -> child FK values collapse to 2 clubs, match_result.Club_ID likewise.
Tiny original tables (5-14 rows) mean original_values pool is small; 5-with-replacement sampling gives near-full coverage but little diversity.
Number perturbation (+-1,+-2) on ints keeps values near the huge random base, not near original small ints — implausible Votes/Points/Gold.
Likely FN driver: implausible huge ints and gibberish strings make WHERE/HAVING filters return empty, so gold and mutant both empty -> missed kill.
Likely FP driver: FK collapse to 2 clubs and PK-duplicate drops create accidental ties/duplicates that make distinct queries agree.
Start_year/Starting_year as INT get huge ints, so year-range predicates (Start_year>2000) become trivially true/false — implausible.
No Date/Time/Bool/Bit columns: only Number and String fuzzers active; Date/Time quirks untested on this DB.
